text: Good afternoon. I'd like to call the October 14th, 2025 school board work session to order. First, we have a report from the school board audit and finance committee from Dr. Perkins. Good afternoon, Madam Chair, Dr. Murray, and board members. My name is Terry Perkins, and I'm chair of the audit and finance advisory committee. So I'm here today to report on activities we've

done in the past year and recommendations for going forward. We have five seats on this committee, One from each district, as you know, two will be filled soon, I think one very soon. Joining me currently on the committee are Mr. Decker and Dr. Mallory.

The stated purpose of this group is to assist the board in its oversight responsibilities for budgeting, financial reporting, internal control systems, and audit processes. We meet about nine times per year to discuss those issues and to hear presentations from staff and to receive reports and information.

This year, we again spent time hearing updates on relevant and timely matters that relate to audit and finance. These included the continued work on the enterprise resource planning system and information that is also provided to the board on things like budget needs and development, our division plans and successes.

We also hear updates from the Chesterfield County staff that include the fraud, waste, and abuse hotline updates, audit plans, and completions, and if recommendations were implemented. We discussed finance-related matters that come up annually or occasionally, and this year those included student activity funds report, information from the county's director of procurement, updates of the SRP, non-resident tuition, and some federal funding information.

Of course, audits constitute a significant amount of our time and attention. This past year, there were audits done by the Chesterfield Internal Audit Department that fell on the school side that included being on school attendance, on volunteers in our schools, and an audit on the procurement and credit card processes.

We appreciated hearing the detailed manner in which these audits were done and what the findings were. We learned of recommendations that come from those findings and what departments within CCPS must implement some sort of action or change. Recommendations from the audits noted here involve many CCPS staff, including divisions, departments, or offices of school social work, equity and student support, safety and security, and finance. Some recommendations can be implemented fairly quickly. For instance, within the school year, others would be more complex work and might take through 2027 to

complete. Based on discussions we've had through the year, we would respectfully suggest a couple of areas for the board's attention and financial support. First, the ERP is a tool that can solve many division challenges by integrating processes, automating tasks, and reducing reliance on paper documentation, among other things.

So we see the supreme value of this software and recommend not only full support for the first phase of implementation that is coming soon, but continued attention to what CCPS's finance department deems necessary for the ERP to evolve into a tool that could improve efficiency in even more areas. Staffing to match the needs of the finance issues connected to ERP is vital.

Secondly, as a group that learns of successes and challenges within the district in terms of student needs and budgetary matters, we continue to advocate for an emphasis on raises for our teacher and support staff. It must meet the needs of the moment in which we find ourselves given that there is a teacher shortage and it is real with dire consequences. Teachers have choices both in the local area and beyond when they are deciding where to serve our students.

The AFC hears regularly of the many pools on dollars in our school division so we understand how budget dollars must be spread, often too thinly across so many needs. Yet we, like most stakeholders, realize that the mission and vision of our changing school division is dependent upon our teachers and support staff. So we urge the board to make competitive staff raises a priority in your upcoming budget season. I'll close by relaying our thanks to Bob Meister and Cara Durden and their teams. These skilled leaders in the division and county provide our committee with

important information that allows us to view the work of audit and finance and learn more about how CCPS could be even better. Sometimes teams like these work behind the scenes in school districts, but we know that there is no possible way in which an effective organization could survive without them, so we appreciate their professionalism and hard work. Finally, I would stress that the committee is open to ways in which we can serve you better, so we would welcome your suggestions

for future meeting topics at any time. Thank you. Thank you, Dr. Perkins. Board members, is there any discussion? Mr. Paranto? Thank you, Madam Chair.
